title: typedef, enum and union
summary: typedef gives a type a new name, often used to drop the word struct. enum names a set of integer constants and makes switch statements readable. A union stores one of several types in the same memory, and a tagged union pairs it with an enum saying which one is there.

cards.q: What does typedef struct { int x; } Point; let you write?
cards.a:
Point p; instead of struct ... p;

typedef only adds a name.

cards.q: enum color { RED, GREEN, BLUE }; - what is BLUE?
How big is a union of an int, a double and a char[3]?
cards.a:
The size of the double: the biggest member

All members share the same memory.

cards.q: What is the enum in a tagged union for?
cards.a:
Saying which member currently holds the value

Without it you cannot tell what is stored.
